title: Cheat resistance: server authority audit and abuse tests
description: A dedicated abuse pass over the whole gameplay pipeline: every player-influenced value is server-validated, and a scripted 'cheater' client gets nothing — no speed hacks, no hit claims, no economy duplication, no protocol abuse.
acceptanceCriteria: Abuse test suite (tests/abuse/): a scripted client (raw ws, no game client) attempts each cheat class and gains nothing: (1) position teleport (sends position claims — ignored, the sim integrates from inputs only), (2) hit claims (sends 'I hit' — no such message exists; firing off-rate gains nothing), (3) fire spam (30/s → weapon lock, no damage beyond the rate limit), (4) mine spam (20 mine-ticks/s → server-cadence awards only), (5) sell spam (100 sells/s → rate-limited + idempotent, no credit duplication), (6) warp spam (rapid warp requests → one in flight, queue dropped), (7) message flood (1000 junk messages/s → conn rate-limited, then kicked with a reconnect-required close code), (8) payload abuse (oversized messages > 64 KB rejected, non-JSON rejected, deep nesting > 32 levels rejected)

Economy audit: no sequence of valid messages can create credits or resources from nothing — the only credit sources are sales (TASK-40) and the only resource sources are deposits (TASK-37, bounded); a property test: run 1000 random valid message sequences against a fresh shard, total credits issued ≤ expected from sales, total resources mined ≤ deposit totals
Input sanitization audit: every WS/REST entry point has a zod schema (TASK-64) — a test enumerates all routes/handlers and asserts each has a schema (no undocumented entry points)
Rate-limit audit: every stateful handler (fire, mine, sell, interact, chat, warp, join) has an explicit limiter (TASK-65) — a test asserts the limiter registry covers the handler list
All abuse tests green: every cheat attempt is neutralized with the correct rejection (no crashes, no log spam — rejections logged at debug, kicks at info)
npm run test green including the property test (1000 sequences, < 60 s runtime)

steps.details: tests/abuse/rawClient.ts: a minimal ws client that sends arbitrary message objects (no game logic); each abuse test is one scenario: connect, claim a test callsign, attempt, assert neutralization (state unchanged + correct error).
Implement the 8 scenarios per acceptance; assert final server state (credits, resources, positions, entity counts) matches the honest baseline exactly.

Random valid-sequence generator (seeded): pick random actions from the validated message set, apply to a fresh shard (in-memory sqlite), after 1000 sequences assert the invariants (credits bounded by sales, resources bounded by deposits, no negative balances, entity counts within caps).

Schema-coverage test (enumerate routes + ws handlers, assert zod schema presence via a registry — TASK-64's schemas are registered at module load); limiter-coverage test (same pattern for TASK-65). Run full suite.

technicalNotes: This task changes no production code unless an abuse test finds a hole — if it does, fix the hole in the owning module and keep the abuse test as the regression guard.
The property test is the long-term guard: it runs in CI and would catch a future economy bug that creates value from nothing.
Kick close code: 4001 'rate-limited-kick' (documented in the protocol, TASK-69).
